options: An applicant must be at least 21, but there is no upper application age limit.
An applicant can apply at 18 if they have already held a licence for three years.
Anyone aged over 65 is automatically excluded from applying.
The badge must be visible while travelling to collect a passenger, unless the driver is exempt.
The badge is needed only after a passenger has entered the vehicle.
Keeping the badge hidden in a wallet meets the normal display requirement.
Drivers aged 65 and over must have a medical assessment every year.
Drivers aged 65 and over need a medical only every third year.
Medical assessments are no longer needed once a driver reaches 65.
A change of home address should be reported to TfL within 21 days.
A driver need only update the home address when the PHV licence is renewed.
Updating the DVLA address removes any need to notify TfL of the move.
A fixed penalty that results in driving-licence points must be reported to TfL.
A driver can rely entirely on police to tell TfL about penalty points.
Every parking PCN automatically results in the driver's licence being revoked.
Applicants must use the company specified by TfL to arrange the required DBS certificate.
Any certificate arranged privately must be accepted, regardless of TfL's process.
An ordinary reference from an employer replaces the enhanced criminal-record check.
Licence discs should remain fixed when the vehicle is being used privately.
The discs should be removed before every private journey and reattached afterwards.
A driver may carry badly damaged discs in a pocket instead of replacing them.
An owner must tell TfL within 72 hours of collision damage affecting safety, performance, appearance or comfort.
Collision damage needs reporting only if the vehicle can no longer be driven.
An owner may wait until the next annual inspection to report any collision damage.
The operator's booking must reach the driver before the passenger enters the vehicle.
A passenger may enter first and ask the driver to arrange a booking afterwards.
A street hail is sufficient if the passenger is standing outside the operator's office.
The handbook directs Heathrow passenger collections to an official car park.
PHVs may collect from Heathrow taxi ranks whenever no taxis are waiting.
A Heathrow booking allows a PHV to collect from any convenient road outside a terminal.
The operator agrees the fare or provides an accurate estimate before the journey.
TfL fixes the price of each private hire journey using a compulsory PHV tariff.
The fare only needs to be discussed after the passenger reaches the destination.
The operator must arrange an alternative driver or make clear that the accepted booking is cancelled.
A driver can abandon an accepted booking without informing the operator.
Disability alone is a sufficient reason for refusing an accepted booking.
Checking the passenger's name and destination before boarding helps prevent them entering the wrong vehicle.
The driver should assume that the first person approaching is the booked passenger.
Identity checks should be postponed until the journey has ended.
An unconscious passenger without anyone to help requires a 999 call and support until emergency services arrive.
The driver should leave an unconscious passenger without contacting emergency services.
A driver should guess a destination for someone unable to confirm it because of intoxication.
If attempts to calm violence fail, the driver should leave the threatening situation safely.
The driver must remain within reach of an aggressor until the fare is settled.
Arguing more forcefully is the recommended next step when calm discussion fails.
Near misses should be recorded and reported as well as incidents that actually happen.
Only incidents that cause a physical injury should be recorded.
Witness details are irrelevant when recording a threat or assault.
The CCTV notice should be visible to passengers without obstructing the driver's view.
A notice hidden in the glovebox meets the passenger visibility requirement.
The notice should cover the driver's view if this makes it more prominent to passengers.
Passenger contact details obtained through a booking should not be used for personal or social messages.
Completing a journey gives the driver permission to send the passenger social messages later.
A driver may use a passenger's number privately whenever the passenger was friendly.
Sexual activity between a driver and passenger is unacceptable even when both agree.
Sexual activity becomes acceptable if the passenger suggests it first.
A passenger may offer sexual activity instead of the fare if the driver accepts.
A driver must not display or share sexual material with passengers.
Sexual material may be displayed if the driver thinks it is harmless.
The driver's good intentions alone determine whether passengers should accept sexual behaviour.
A sign allowing taxis does not by itself give a PHV the same access.
Every PHV has the same road access as a licensed taxi.
Carrying a pre-booked passenger lets a PHV ignore a taxi-only restriction.
Permission to pick up a passenger does not allow waiting indefinitely where restrictions apply.
Arriving early for a booking automatically permits waiting on restricted yellow lines.
Hazard lights allow a PHV to wait wherever it could briefly let a passenger board.
A camera-recorded offence can produce a valid postal PCN without a notice on the windscreen.
A PCN is always invalid unless attached to the windscreen by an officer.
Only parking offences can result in a PCN; moving-traffic offences cannot.
The overnight red-route cashpoint exception allows no more than five minutes of waiting.
The cashpoint exception allows a driver to wait for thirty minutes whenever a passenger asks.
The cashpoint exception overrides the prohibition on stopping on pedestrian-crossing zig-zags.
A driver must stay within the speed limit and choose a speed suited to the conditions.
Driving at the posted limit is always safe regardless of weather.
A passenger running late authorises the driver to exceed the speed limit.
When the correct child seat is unavailable, the handbook's under-three exception applies to a rear seat.
The described child-seat exception allows an under-three to travel on the driver's lap.
The described exception permits a child without the correct restraint to travel in any front seat.
Placing a cradled device in the wiper-swept windscreen area can be an offence.
Every device is acceptable on the windscreen provided it helps with navigation.
Checking the view is unnecessary if devices were installed by the operator.
A driver should not begin a journey when already tired and should plan regular breaks.
Driving faster is the recommended way to deal with tiredness.
Familiarity with a route removes the need for rest breaks.
A PHV must not enter the cycle advanced stop box when the light is red.
A PHV may enter the box on red whenever no cyclist is present.
The box is reserved for PHVs when they carry a booked passenger.
Tyre size, speed and weight ratings must be appropriate for the make and model of the vehicle.
Any tyre is suitable if its price is low enough and it can be fitted to the rim.
Tyre ratings do not matter on a vehicle used only for private hire journeys.
A tyre must be replaced when its tread has worn to the wear indicators.
A tyre at the wear indicators can stay in service until it punctures.
Painting over the wear indicators is an acceptable alternative to replacement.
The driver should offer assistance and wait for the passenger to accept it.
The driver should grab a passenger's arm before asking whether help is wanted.
Assistance needs can always be inferred accurately from a passenger's appearance.
A passenger may have a disability that is not visibly apparent and still need assistance.
Only passengers with a clearly visible disability may ask for help.
If a passenger looks healthy, the driver should disregard requests for assistance.
A passenger must not be charged extra because they use a wheelchair.
A wheelchair surcharge is required whenever securing the chair takes additional time.
A wheelchair user must always transfer to a passenger seat even in a designated accessible PHV.
Assistance dogs may be different breeds and need not match the handbook pictures.
Only dogs of the breeds pictured in the handbook can qualify as assistance dogs.
A driver can obtain an assistance-dog exemption merely because they prefer not to carry dogs.
A medical condition may justify applying to TfL for an exemption, rather than declaring one independently.
A driver becomes automatically exempt as soon as they say they have a medical condition.
An operator's verbal permission replaces the need for TfL to grant an exemption.
For an unaccompanied child, the operator should know the situation and the driver should know who will meet the child.
An unaccompanied child's receiving adult need not be identified before the journey.
Safeguarding is solely the responsibility of police and social workers, never PHV drivers.
A disclosure of abuse should be reported to the operator and police.
A driver should promise to conceal a passenger's disclosure of abuse from everyone.
A driver must prove the abuse personally before reporting a concern.
An anonymous report should still contain as much useful information as possible.
An anonymous report must omit details about the incident.
A driver must give their own name before any safeguarding concern can be reported.
One passenger's personal details should not be shared with other passengers.
Ridesharing automatically allows the driver to disclose everyone's home routine.
A shared fare gives passengers the right to obtain each other's private contact details.
